claim: arch_release.md: 'A tag-triggered GoReleaser build turning a version tag into a GitHub Release... The GoReleaser configuration and the release workflow are the source of truth for how a release is built; this leaf states the contract they must keep.' The ReleasePipeline component (649f5268a2b2) is scoped to an implementer bead, which assumes an implementer box can author and land the release GitHub Actions workflow file the same way it lands any other file in a normal feature-branch PR.
authoritative_source: The push transport itself: portitor is the only GitHub credential holder and forwards accepted implementer branches to GitHub upstream. Its GitHub token does not carry the `workflow` OAuth scope, so GitHub itself rejects any push that creates or updates a file under `.github/workflows/` before it ever reaches a PR — independent of content, signing, or role. Implementer boxes are restricted to `portitor pr` only, so there is no self-service recovery (`portitor reconcile --repo <name>`, the error's own suggested recovery, is not in the implementer's allowed command set).
evidence: This exact defect was already reported twice on this bead (drifts/drift-spexmachina-ow43.3.json, merged via PR #233) and triaged closed via PR #234 with the note 'The reported transport rejection (PAT lacking workflow scope) is fixed on the credential itself; the spec's contract was correct as written.' This cycle re-implemented the component from scratch on a fresh branch off the post-#234 origin/main (commit 0687f49), built .goreleaser.yaml and .github/workflows/release.yml per arch_release.md's build-matrix, trust-chain, and release-assets sections, and pushed. The push to the internal git server succeeded, but the upstream forward failed with the identical error as before: 'remote: portitor: forward refs/heads/spexmachina-ow43.3 -> upstream FAILED: ... remote rejected ... (refusing to allow a Personal Access Token to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/release.yml` without `workflow` scope) ... error: failed to push some refs ... (recover with: portitor reconcile --repo <name>)'. The credential fix #234 recorded as applied does not hold: the constraint is reproduced fresh, on a clean branch, immediately after the claimed fix. This blocks the bead's own contract structurally and blocks every component in this module whose deliverable includes a workflow file: ReleasePipeline (this bead), and — by the same mechanism — CIPipeline (spexmachina-ow43.2, arch_ci.md) and SpecGate (spexmachina-ow43.1, arch_spec_gate.md) once they reach an implementer.
proposed_fix: Re-verify the credential fix from #234 directly against a `.github/workflows/*` push before closing this again — the prior triage closed on the credential owner's report without an implementer re-test, and that report was evidently wrong or the fix did not persist (token rotated back, scope not actually granted, wrong credential updated, etc.). Alternatively, adopt the drift report's original (b) option: move workflow-file authorship out of the implementer path entirely — pre-author .github/workflows/release.yml (and arch_ci.md's, arch_spec_gate.md's) in the authoring loop, same read-only-for-implementers treatment spec/ already gets — and scope ReleasePipeline down to the non-workflow artifacts (.goreleaser.yaml, which pushes without issue).
